audit.whatIsWrong: Every chart row disagreed across layers (full read Skill x5 then Kassadin, Kassadin; content read Orianna x5, Skill, Orianna), and the packet flags the content chart as contradicting a 45.02% win rate by giving Orianna 6 of 7 stages.
audit.why: Both layers were partly right. Orianna genuinely owns levels 1 through 5 — Kassadin has no waveclear, Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1 and only 400 range. What neither chart said honestly is that the lane inverts once Riftwalk ranks up, which is exactly what a 45.02% win rate over 864 games reflects.
audit.corrected: Orianna for levels 1-5, Skill at level 6 and first item, Kassadin at two items — resolves the packet defect and the cross-layer split together.

audit.whatIsWrong: No spike text used Riftwalk's actual rank cooldowns, which are the whole shape of this matchup.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1, 3.5s at rank 2 and 2s at rank 3, 500 range, with stacking mana cost and stacking damage. That descending number is why your pre-6 dominance decays into a losing late.
audit.corrected: Ranks written into the level 6, first item and two-item rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it; two Do's/Don'ts bodies were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad pastes under unrelated titles.
audit.why: The interactions that matter: Null Sphere interrupts channels and leaves him a magic-damage shield, so it eats your poke and cancels casts; Force Pulse charges off spells cast nearby, so your own Q-W spam feeds it; Riftwalk is a blink, not a dash, and Dissonance's slow field only taxes the walk between blinks. Your E is 9s and your R 110s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: All four fields rewritten with the real numbers and the real interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nether Blade's auto-attack reset was never mentioned.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags it: his combo opens on an auto reset, so the wind-up animation is the cue to step back — there is no cast to react to.
